papers.title_en: eSharp: Diffusion-based Sharp Monocular Metric Event-to-Depth Estimation
papers.authors: Qiushi Dai, Aniket Dashpute, Yuhao Liu, Rishubh Parihar, Guha Balakrishnan, Ashok Veeraraghavan
papers.evidence: 基于事件相机和扩散先验的单目度量深度估计
papers.tldr: 事件相机单目深度估计在快速运动和高动态范围场景中具有潜力，但真实事件数据仅有稀疏LiDAR深度监督，难以实现稠密高精度预测。eSharp复用预训练扩散先验进行纯事件单目度量深度估计，并通过跨模态蒸馏引入由共配准帧相机生成且经LiDAR校准的稠密伪标签来训练模型。实验表明其在度量深度精度和空间保真度上均优于既往事件到深度基线，输出更锐利。该工作将扩散模型确立为事件驱动三维感知的有力基础。
papers.abstract_en: Depth perception is fundamental for autonomous navigation, industrial inspection, and mixed-reality systems. It often operates under strict constraints on power and form factor. In such cases, monocular depth estimation (MDE) is often used. Even as recent advances continue to improve monocular depth quality, conventional frame-based MDE systems remain challenged by fast motion and high-dynamic-range scenes. This work introduces eSharp, an MDE framework that addresses these problems using an event camera. eSharp repurposes pretrained diffusion priors for event-only MDE and produces accurate metric depth with unparalleled sharpness on real data. Real-world event datasets provide only sparse LiDAR depth maps for ground-truth supervision, making dense prediction challenging. We address this limitation through cross-modal distillation, using LiDAR-calibrated dense pseudo-labels generated from a spatially co-registered frame camera to train eSharp. Experiments show that eSharp outperforms prior event-to-depth baselines in both metric-depth accuracy and spatial fidelity, establishing diffusion models as a promising foundation for event-driven 3D perception.

papers.title_en: Extrapolation Matters: Sparse-Only Depth Completion Beyond LiDAR Coverage
papers.authors: Maximilian Jansen, Gasser Elazab, Praveen Kulkarni
papers.evidence: 冻结的单目深度基础模型结合稀疏激光雷达预测度量深度
papers.tldr: 真实相机-LiDAR系统常因重叠有限、遮挡和视场受限而缺失覆盖外深度，现有评测也易掩盖外推能力。论文仅用原始单帧稀疏LiDAR监督，冻结单目深度基础模型，逐帧对齐稀疏几何，并用细化模块融合对齐先验与稀疏锚点预测稠密度量深度。作者还提出高频法向一致性损失及区分覆盖内外的评测协议。结果显示覆盖外精度较强、覆盖内保持竞争力，为多传感器系统部署单目基础先验提供实用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Extrapolation beyond LiDAR coverage is an important yet under-evaluated challenge of depth completion. In real camera--LiDAR systems, partial sensor overlap, occlusions, and limited field coverage often leave large image regions weakly observed or completely unobserved by LiDAR. Thus, we investigate depth completion in this beyond-coverage regime using only sparse supervision from raw single-sweep LiDAR, without dense depth labels, LiDAR accumulation, or pseudo-LiDAR generation. Our approach leverages a frozen monocular depth foundation model, lightweight per-frame alignment to sparse LiDAR geometry, and a refinement module that fuses the aligned prior with sparse LiDAR anchors to predict dense metric depth. To regularize learning under raw sparse supervision, we introduce a high-frequency normal-consistency loss defined as the image-space gradient of the per-pixel normal cosine discrepancy. This term penalizes spatial variation in scalar angular error; it does not directly match changes in neighboring normal vectors. We further introduce an evaluation protocol that explicitly separates LiDAR-supported and beyond-coverage regions, revealing extrapolative behavior that conventional depth-completion metrics can obscure. Our method achieves strong depth accuracy beyond LiDAR coverage while remaining competitive in LiDAR-covered regions, providing a practical way to deploy monocular foundation priors in multi-sensor systems.
